messages.content: What is the largest planet in the universe?

message.content:
We don’t yet have a definitive “largest planet” in the entire universe—our knowledge is limited to what we can observe from Earth and our solar system. Within our own Solar System, Jupiter is the biggest planet, with a diameter of about 142,000 km. In terms of exoplanets (planets orbiting other stars), the record‑holder is still uncertain because many candidates are either very large gas giants or even brown dwarfs that sit on the boundary between planets and stars.

One of the most massive exoplanets discovered so far is **HD 100546 b**, a protoplanet still forming around a young star. It has an estimated mass of roughly 10–20 times that of Jupiter, making it one of the heaviest planetary‑mass objects we’ve found. However, its exact nature is still debated—it could be a massive planet or a low‑mass brown dwarf.

In short, the largest confirmed planet in our Solar System is Jupiter, while the largest known exoplanet candidate is HD 100546 b, though its status as a planet versus a brown dwarf remains under study. As exoplanet surveys continue, we may discover even larger planetary bodies—or find that the definition of “planet” needs to be refined.
